title: Nightshift KV + Batch Drift Scrub — 2027-02-19
content:
Summary:
During the 02/17-02/19 nightshifts we tracked a correlated drift in KV cache hit-rate and batch-size distribution that caused a measurable p95 latency bump for short chat-turn workloads. This doc captures the hypothesis loop, quick experiments, and next steps. Intended as a quick, informal scrub log for follow-ups in the morning.

What happened (short):
- Friday 02/12 a small kernel change (PR 1987) adjusted the attention-kernel prefetch window to improve long-context throughput.
- Over the past week, nightshift telemetry showed median batch size increasing from ~6 -> ~10 and KV hit-rate dropping from ~88% -> ~71% for the same workload class (short turns, frequent restarts).
- p50 unaffected; p95 rose from 210ms -> 360ms for rtx-a100 pools serving chat-s1 short-turn routes. CPU on CPU-proxy and GPU utilization still within expected bounds.
- Rough hypothesis: prefetch-window change increases prefill behavior for new requests, producing more prefix differences and preventing KV reuse; combined with new request coalescing timing, we increased micro-batching of single-turn requests which increased scheduling jitter at 2nd-stage kernels.

Data & quick checks performed:
- Confirmed PR 1987 merged 02/09 and rolled to night pools 02/11 via rollout v1.24.
- Queried metrics: kv_cache.hit_rate by route for last 14 days. See linked artifact RDW-4321 for raw query ids.
- Captured batch size histogram (sampled): 02/10 baseline: p50=6 p75=9 p95=14; 02/17 evening: p50=9 p75=13 p95=20.
- Traced a sample slow request: micro-batch size 18, multiple small prefixes resulted in multiple KV lookups; fuse step couldn't reuse KV due to offset mismatch (see trace id slack thread).

Experiments run (night):
1) TTL rollback on ephemeral session cache (rollback from 90s -> 30s) — quick A/B on one serving island (island-7). Result: KV hit increased ~6% within 30m but batch distribution not fixed.
2) Kernel prefetch backoff (temporary flag to reduce prefetch aggressiveness by 40%) — tested in staging and then in island-7. Result: batch p50 lowered to 7, p95 lowered ~30ms; KV hit-rate improved marginally.
3) Coalescer timing adjustment (hold-open window +20ms) — trying to increase coalescing of tiny requests. Result: increased batch sizes further (bad for latency), reverted.
4) Introduced short-turn detection path to prioritize KV reuse (prototype flag). Observed promising traces where reused KV avoided duplicate attention compute; still flaky due to header parity checks.

Immediate conclusions:
- Root cause likely interaction of prefetch scheduling + coalescer timing that increases variety of prefixes seen by KV cache and changes batch mix.
- Two lever classes: reduce unnecessary prefetches OR make KV reuse tolerant to small offset shifts.
- Quick rollback of PR 1987 is undesirable (regression for long-context throughput) — prefer targeted mitigations.

Action plan (owners + due dates):
- Marcus: roll a conservative prefetch-limiter flag in night pools (island-7, island-9) and monitor 24h. Due: 2027-02-20.
- Ava: implement KV key-normalization shim (normalize small offset diffs) as a hotfix branch and run canary on 1/4 traffic. Due: 2027-02-24.
- Priya: add more granular tracing in coalescer to capture request arrival deltas and header parity rates. Due: 2027-02-21.
- Omar: coordinate with infra to allocate two more ephemeral islands for isolated AB-tests (island-12 & island-13). Due: 2027-02-20.
- Lin: produce a nightly dashboard with per-route kv_hit_rate, batch_size_p50/p95, and kernel-fuse-failures. Due: 2027-02-22.

Standup snippets (nightshift, raw notes):
- 02/17 23:12 Marcus: saw first p95 spike; rolled prefetch limiter on island-7 (quick). Noticed trace patterns showing offset-mismatch.
- 02/18 01:47 Ava: started KV-normalization prototype; small PoC passes unit tests but needs perf guardrails.
- 02/18 03:05 Priya: coalescer hold-open test inflated batches -> reverted; collecting arrival-time histograms.
- 02/18 05:30 Omar: infra stood up islands 12/13; ready for canaries.
- 02/19 00:02 Lin: dashboard skeleton pushed; missing some telemetry labels.

Open questions / unresolved:
- Are we seeing any client-side behavior contributing? (clients may be sending slightly different session tokens causing cache fragmentation) — need to query frontend logs.
- What was the exact sequence that made prefetch change necessary? Was it compensating for another regression on long-contexts — if we disable, are we re-introducing that regression elsewhere?
- How brittle is KV key-normalization wrt security/audit requirements? We need a security review before enabling broadly.

Notes to self / heuristics learned:
- Night telemetry is good for catching mid-roll interactions; keep small islands for quick AB.
- Avoid simultaneous changes to coalescer and kernel prefetch in the same roll (we learned this the hard way).
- Small increases in median batch size can hide downstream p95 degradation because they affect scheduling jitter non-linearly.

Follow-ups for morning sync:
- 09:00 triage: review early metrics from prefetch-limiter on islands 7/9.
- 10:30 eng-wide: propose KV-normalization design + perf targets.
- Prepare rollback playbook if prefetch-limiter causes long-context regressions.

Appendix (quick links & traces):
- GH PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1987
- Trace samples: trace-ids [trace-20270217-09, trace-20270218-03] (slack thread)
- Jira: RDW-4321 (kv/batch investigation)

End of nightshift scrub.
(Informal — intended to be iterated on during the day; add more artifacts to linked_artifacts as they surface.)
